card.title: The Rule You Broke
card.instruction: Treat a past breach of rule or custom as unfinished business. Let every present exception reopen the question of what was damaged.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're letting guests use the good mugs now?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only because the other mugs are packed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: When I used one, you called it a breach of trust.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I replaced the mug. Will you tell them that when you do your usual warning about letting me carry things?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 questions the new good-mug exception, A3 recalls being judged untrustworthy, and A5 distinguishes replaced property from an ongoing reputational warning.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's packed-mug explanation causes A3's earlier-trust comparison; B4's breakage correction causes A5's replacement and warning request.

relationship.evidence: B2 has a practical reason for the exception and B4 names the factual difference in A's earlier use.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's damage explanation to ask why repairing that damage has not repaired the public label.

specificity.evidence: A1-B2 establish guests using special mugs because ordinary ones are packed.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's include-the-replacement-in-the-warning request is earned by B4's broken-mug fact.
